question.problem:
Consider the following predicates:

$\qquad$ $P(x):$ $x\in\mathbb {Z}^{-}$ $\qquad$ $Q(x):$ $x$ is negative

Which of the following expresses the conditional predicate $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x)?$

I. Whenever $x$ is negative, then $x\in\mathbb {Z}^{-}$

II. $x$ is negative whenever $x\in\mathbb {Z}^{-}$

III. $x$ is negative, provided that $x\in\mathbb {Z}^{-}$
question.worked_solution:
Given that the implication $P \Rightarrow Q$ is true, we have the following:

- Whenever $P,$ then $Q$

- $Q$ whenever $P$

- $Q,$ provided that $P$

With that in mind, let's examine the given options.

- Option I reads
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14272126/assets/21fd3acc1e0a8862b0010d28252278e204bfe6c25abb66aed01f31cc0a565642.svg)
which corresponds to $Q(x) \Rightarrow P(x).$ $\:{\color{red}\times}$

- Option II reads
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14272126/assets/4436567914aa607eae98ac50a467d6d6be1715d7b1f9cdfa0f907dc0df8b99ba.svg)
which corresponds to $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x).$ $\:{\color{green}\checkmark}$

- Option III reads
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14272126/assets/305d426cb7c241d68ab4576848ae519429b58e3ae655cb65c23dc74c09d0722e.svg)
which corresponds to $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x).$ $\:{\color{green}\checkmark}$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
